translation: The Zang Qi Fa Shi Lun (臟氣法時論) says: When the kidney suffers from dryness, urgently eat acrid things to moisten it. Now cold things belong to yin and can nourish water and drain fire; hot things belong to yang and can nourish fire and consume water. Now that the kidney water can no longer overcome the heart fire, then both upper and lower are hot—how can one use hot drugs to nourish the kidney water and wish to make it overcome the heart fire? Is this not a great error! Again, as for thirst from heat binding in the stomach and large intestine, the Yin Yang Bie Lun (陰陽別論) says: When one yang is bound, it is called wasting (消). The commentary says: When the two yang are bound, both the stomach and the large intestine are heat-bound.
translator_notes: 臟氣法時論/陰陽別論 kept as chapter names; 一陽/二陽 rendered 'one yang'/'two yang'.
